props.title: Grey Gardens
props.initialSlug: Reclusive socialites survive in decaying Hamptons mansion

sections.content: Grey Gardens revolutionized documentary filmmaking by turning its lens on American aristocracy in decline. The Maysles brothers captured the fascinating codependency between "Big Edie" and "Little Edie" Beale - Jackie Kennedy's aunt and cousin - living in squalor in their decaying East Hampton mansion. The film's direct cinema approach lets the Beales' eccentric personalities and devastating fall from grace unfold naturally, influencing countless documentaries like Crumb (1994) and The Queen of Versailles (2012).

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond documentary into narrative features exploring isolated, codependent relationships. Whatever Happened to Baby Jane? (1962) shares similar themes of sisterly dysfunction in faded glamour, while Sunset Boulevard (1950) examines another reclusive former socialite unable to let go of past glory. The Beales became unlikely fashion icons, with Little Edie's improvisational "revolutionary costumes" inspiring designers and The New York Times declaring her a "fashion genius." SUBHEAD: Legacy and Cultural Impact

Grey Gardens spawned multiple adaptations, including a 2006 Broadway musical and the HBO film starring Drew Barrymore. The documentary's unflinching yet empathetic portrayal of mental illness and family dysfunction influenced later works like The Wolfpack (2015) and Finding Vivian Maier (2013). The Beales' quotable dialogue and memorable personalities made them cult figures, referenced everywhere from RuPaul's Drag Race to Documentary Now!'s loving parody "Sandy Passage" (2015).
